title: Feature-snapshot inventory section on /desk (the observer's build truth)
hypothesis: GET /research/desk/micro/snapshots (+ /snapshots/runs) is a second Data Contract row with zero UI and zero MCP readers, so the 18 legacy snapshots J-02 built -- and their verified identities, algo/format versions, quote_size_unit stamps and fallback/unknown fractions -- are only reachable by curl; a read-only inventory section would make the observer's own build truth visible beside Microscope Readiness. Ranked BELOW the graduation proposal because snapshot rows are per-dataset and therefore sit closer to the opaque-pool anti-goal (a per-shard snapshot list must never let an unexposed vault shard be identified), so it needs a full TR-2 inference sweep design before it is safe to build, and it is a build inventory rather than a research result.
journey_sketch: Render a read-only Snapshots section on /desk reading GET /research/desk/micro/snapshots verbatim, with the TR-2 inference sweep extended over it and no per-shard identity of any unexposed pool member.

title: GET /research/desk/micro/snapshots discloses what it excludes (withheld_excluded + stale_excluded)
hypothesis: micro_snapshots.list_snapshot_meta drops rows twice over WITHOUT a count: it skips every unresolved-pool (withheld) dataset id (micro_snapshots.py:376-381) and it silently drops any stored meta that fails load-time identity re-verification (its own docstring: 'silently excluded'), so the route can serve [] while 18 .meta.json files sit on disk and no reader can tell 'never built' from 'built then invalidated by an algo/format/feature-source/fingerprint move' from 'withheld because it belongs to the sealed pool'. Every sibling enumerator already discloses its exclusions -- GET /research/datasets serves sealed_withheld, GET .../snapshots/compute serves withheld_excluded, readiness renders micro-readiness-withheld-excluded -- so this one route is the odd one out, and a UI section over it would be misleading rather than honest. Fix additively at the one owner via the shared exclude_withheld choke point (never a per-snapshot-file-derived count, which would leak sealed-pool build state).
journey_sketch: Serve withheld_excluded and stale_excluded (computed after the withheld filter, by the existing choke point) beside `snapshots`, and render them in the new Feature Snapshots section -- promoted jointly with micro-snapshots-surface as J-12.

title: Re-run the promotion sweep on the grown, seal-filtered corpus and publish state/pnl-scan.json (workstream W3)
hypothesis: The proposer's own primary screen has no input: state/pnl-scan.json does not exist in this session and the post-goal hook never wrote one, so no data-backed candidate can be screened at all. Meanwhile the registered dataset library has grown from the founding 1 train / 1 hold-out pair to 98 datasets, of which ~17 (11 train / 6 hold-out, measured from .data/dataset_index.db minus the unresolved-pool ids implied by vault_shard_ledger + vault_universe_ledger) are outside the sealed J-06 pool and therefore legally sweepable; the one registered candidate profile (faster_warmup) has never been evaluated against that corpus, so it is genuinely unknown whether hold-out n now reaches the configured promotion minimum (5) for the first time in the project's history. pnl_scan already calls exclude_withheld (pnl_scan.py:248) so the sweep cannot touch a sealed shard, and authorize_promotion is consulted BEFORE append_validation_row with no bypass, so with zero corroborated Referee hypotheses the run can neither move the champion pointer nor append a ledger row -- it can only produce the report. NOT promoted this cycle: it is a multi-hour real-corpus compute (17 datasets x 2 profiles of full tick replay, several shards ~0.5 GB) on a host under mandatory guard caps, it is an operator-attended act the session's standing bars currently withhold, and the Rapid-Microscope era freezes the pnl_scan/profiles/champion family -- so it belongs to workstream W3 (consolidation) or the next era's opening, not to a lean iteration of this one.
journey_sketch: Operator-run `python -m app.research.pnl_scan --out runs/<session>/state/pnl-scan.json` over the seal-filtered corpus, then report the per-split net R / net $ / n for faster_warmup vs the champion with the insufficient-sample label wherever n < 5 -- measurement only, promotion structurally impossible without a Referee certificate.

title: Recorder progress/runs is the last Data-Contract row with zero readers -- OBSERVED, DECLINED, not promoted
hypothesis: Survey finding, recorded so a future cycle does not re-discover it without the counter-argument. 'Recorder job + tranche progress/runs' (goal.md Product Shape Data Contract, owner app/research/tick_recorder.py, endpoints GET /research/desk/micro/recorder/compute and GET .../recorder/runs) is now the ONLY micro Data-Contract row with no reader on either surface: measured by grep, zero hits for 'micro/recorder' in apps/frontend/lib/api.ts and apps/frontend/app/desk/page.tsx, and no recorder tool in tests/test_mcp_server.py EXPECTED_TOOLS (28 tools). Every other row now has both (readiness/scout/walkforward/vault since J-08, graduation since J-11, snapshots since J-12). DECLINED -- deliberately NOT promoted to a journey, on four grounds measured this cycle, not asserted: (1) it would render permanently empty AND contradict the record. The real store has no micro_recorder_runs directory (read_run_log returns [] for a missing path), because the J-06 tranche was executed by apps/backend/scripts/j06_operator.py calling tick_recorder.run_tick_recording directly and writing its own operator report -- reports/j06-tranche/recording-runs.json, 5 runs / 80 recorded pairs / 2 failed pairs -- so a new section would print 'no recorder runs' on a desk whose Validation Vault shows 21 sealed shards from those very runs. That is the first empty state in this era that would misdescribe what happened, which is the opposite of the honest-empty-state design rule. (2) tick_recorder/micro_snapshots.read_run_log documents this log as 'convenience bookkeeping, never a claim of record' -- the record of record is the datasets, the vault shard ledger and the readiness aggregates, all three already surfaced. (3) the live-progress half is the era's most leak-sensitive path: owner ruling r5 (assumptions.md 2026-08-18) plus TR-32 removed every outcome-typed field from GET .../recorder/compute precisely because an observer POLLING across a single-chunk advance reconstructed a run; a page that auto-polls that route is that threat model, and designing it safely is not a lean iteration. (4) nothing can fill it inside this session: the standing bars are 'no new real tape, no sealed-shard reveal/assign, no studies on the real corpus', and the era reports the ~150-symbol-day gate honestly unmet (80/150) by design (T-7). If a future era runs W1 (recorder top-up, Card 5.2) through the MANAGER/CLI rather than an operator script, this row acquires real content and can be re-scored then -- that is the materially-new evidence guidance section 7 requires.
journey_sketch: Would be: a read-only Recorder Runs section on /desk below Feature Snapshots plus a byte-identical GET proxy tool -- NOT proposed as a journey this cycle (see hypothesis); revisit only after a manager/CLI-driven recording exists.
